cases.sentence: До нее не доеду? – до моей ___ с глазами, как облака?..
cases.explain: «бесстыжей царицы» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "‘Won’t get where? I won't get to Petushki? To her? To my shameless Tsaritsa with eyes like clouds? You're really funny."

cases.sentence: Я раскис, ангелы, в прошлую пятницу, я на ___ ее загляделся, круглый, как небо и земля…
cases.explain: «белый живот» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: "What do you mean? While I live ... what do you mean? Last Friday, it’s true, she wouldn't let me go to see him. Last Friday I went limp, angels, I took to staring at her white belly, round like the sky and the earth. But, today, I'll get there, ifonly I don’t croak. . . killed by fate . . . today I'll be with her and I'll graze among the lilies till morning. But, tomorrow . .

cases.explain: «Бедный мальчик» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The poor kid, the angels sighed.

cases.sentence: Ты еще ни разу сегодня не улыбнулся, как только улыбнешься в ___ – мы отлетим… и уже будем покойны за тебя…
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Oh, no, we can’t ride as far as Petushki. We'll be flying offas soon as you smile. You haven't smiled once today. As soon as you smile for the first time, we’re off.

cases.explain: «Прелестные существа» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "You're lovely creatures, angels. Only why that ‘poor kid’? He’s not a poor kid at all, the little one who knows the letter ~C like his own five fingers, the little one who loves his father as himself.

cases.sentence: Если нож или бритва попадутся ему на глаза – пусть он ими не играет, найди ему ___, Господь.
cases.explain: «другие игрушки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: "Make it, Lord, so that even if he has fallen from the roof or the stove he won’t have broken either his arm or his leg. If he happens to see a knife or a razor, let him not play with them, Lord, please find other playthings for him, Lord. When his mother stokes the fire, which he loves to watch, drag him off to one side, if you can, Lord. It pains me to think that he might get burned. And if he should get sick, let him start getting better the minute he sees me."’

cases.sentence: Он и в ___ был в жару, и даже ямка на щеке вся была в жару, и было диковинно, что вот у такого ничтожества еще может быть жар…
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «у», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Yes, when I arrived the last time, they told me he was asleep; he was sick and had a fever. I drank lemon vodka by his crib and they left me alone with him. He really did have a fever—even the dimple on his cheek was all warm, and it was curious that such a little nothing could have a fever.

cases.sentence: И все, что они говорят – вечно живущие ангелы и умирающие дети, – все так значительно, что я слова их пишу ___, а все, что мы говорим, – махонькими буковками, потому что это более или менее чепуха.
cases.explain: «длинными курсивами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: The way he said that. Everything they say—the eter- nally living angels and eternally dying children—is so important that I feel I should write down the words in flowing longhand, but I would write everything we say in tiny letters, because what we say is more or less nonsense. "T understand, Father."

cases.sentence: Вот и я: разве я не облетаю? разве не противно глядеть, как я ___ все облетаю да облетаю?..
cases.explain: «целыми днями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: ‘Take the dandelion, for instance. It sways in the wind and scatters, and it’s sad to look at it. That’s me, too. I scatter in the wind. Isn’t it disgusting to see how I scatter in the wind for days on end?"’
